mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates economic weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants react to the negative economic signal.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a strong demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following two consecutive quarters of positive GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals supply chain disruptions or reduced economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face production challenges.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a significant INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate signals a strong demand environment and improving labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and UNRATE decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following an increase in HOUST and a decrease in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants interpret this as a sign of economic strength.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances following a significant PAYEMS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over two consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following two consecutive months of CPI increase.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise due to increased sales.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following a significant RSAFS increase.
